sentences.text: Apatoraptor is a genus of caenagnathid dinosaur containing only one known species, A. pennatus.
The specific name pennatus means "feathered" in Latin, based on quill knobs found on the ulna that indicate the animal had wings.
The holotype specimen, the specimen the species is based on, was found in the Horsethief Member of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation from the Campanian period.
The fossil consists of a largely articulated partial skeleton that includes a skull, lower jaws, vertebrae, ribs, shoulder girdle, arm, sternum, belly ribs, and right leg bones.
A theropod skeleton was discovered in 1993 at Drumheller, Alberta, three kilometers west of the Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology.
Research on the fossil resumed in 2008, leading to the discovery that it represented a species previously unknown to science.
The species Apatoraptor pennatus was formally named and described by Gregory F. Funston and Philip John Currie in 2016.
The fossil was further investigated using a CAT-scan to reveal internal details.
Apatoraptor is classified within the family Caenagnathidae and is considered a possible sister species to Elmisaurus.
Apatoraptor is placed within the Oviraptorosauria group, specifically in the family Caenagnathidae, as a possible sister taxon to Elmisaurus.
The only known specimen of Apatoraptor was found in the Campanian-aged Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta.
The Paleobiology Database lists the time range for Apatoraptor as the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
